triage.author: Parker
triage.text: Beautiful building ruined by AI slop pervading the entire experience

triage.author: kirk189
triage.text: First off it’s an absolutely beautiful setting and building and I really wanted to love this place but my disappointment comes from the content. They are more interested in AI slop than actually teaching you much about President Theodore Roosevelt. Very crowded and really didn’t like all the AI

triage.author: Otto Matieque
triage.text: I wanted to take my family to visit the presidential library but it was too expensive.  It cost over a hundred dollars for a family of four to visit  :-(

triage.author: Elliot Bishop
triage.text:
I never thought a presidential library would remind me of Disneyland, but this one does, and not in the good ways.
Pros:
The building and grounds are beautiful, and are worth visiting on their own, which is free.
Narration by Nick Offerman, I can’t think of a better person for the job.
The exhibit does a good job of connecting the past to the present and future at the end.

Cons:
Overcrowded – despite timed entry they are still letting too many people in. You will still have to wait in line to get in (and once inside), which is slow partially due to the optional photo and information entry for the “enhanced experience”.
Too much reliance on technology. All of the tap points make it feel more like a theme park than a museum. Lines form around the stations where you can get your face on an old time photo. The multi-projector video rooms are unnecessarily overwhelming with visuals where a simple well-done video would have been fine. The use of technology is so aggressive it feels uncomfortable against the historical subject matter, especially considering the conservation themes.
I did not expect a new museum to have many original artifacts, and in fact there are a lot of replicas.

It is worth a visit if you need to distract your kids with something (there is a literal playground type fort inside). I would not recommend it to anyone who appreciates traditional museums/history centers/visitor centers where you can meander, read, and observe.

triage.author: Brian O'Connor
triage.text:
Ticket system is clunky. They need to hold back more tickets for each time block so people can walk up and get tickets the day of. Especially considering its in a location of the country that most people are only passing through maybe once in their life. We had to change our travel plans because of the ticket system.

The library itself is an AI data gathering center surrounded by a few boards of information about Teddy Roosevelt. They ask for your personal information and only tell you its to add to your experience while going through the exhibits. I asked several times what this meant and the guy refused to answer my question and got very frustrated with me for wanting to know.

After going through the library its 100% unnecessary to give your info for the AI slop in the exhibits (imo). It seems the library was designed for young kids and people with very short attention spans. The use of AI generated self portraits felt like just a cute distraction and was in no way a meaningful part of learning about Teddy. The gift shop or lobby would have been a better place for those stations. It would have lessened the crowds just standing and taking up space.

Most of the AI stuff interferes with people who are actually trying to read the information panels. At one point I was tying to read while people walked in front of me that were only there doing an AI scavenger hunt with their wrist bands that made loud bird calls in the room we were in. That was very distracting and frustrating to my experience.

The other AI stations offered very little in terms of adding depth to the museum. All in all this is a pretty sad representation of Teddy Roosevelt and the things he advocated for.

The library feels like a "must stop" thing to see given its location but lacks a lot of substance.

triage.author: G M G
triage.text: One star for the outdoors and the architecture which was great. Otherwise it’s just ai bullshit with replicas of the real things everywhere. I can’t in good faith recommend anyone go to this place. It’s a Presidental library that is unfit for such a president as Teddy Roosevelt. There was no heart or soul put into really anything besides the outdoor parts and the architecture.

triage.author: Benjamin S.
triage.text: Hit up several presidential libraries on my travels--Lincoln, Reagan, Nixon--and never once needed a timed ticket. Just showed up and went in. Then I drove way out to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in the middle of North Dakota, and they turned me away at the door because I didn't have a reservation. Twenty-six bucks to get in and not even close to busy. No flexibility, no accommodation, just a flat no. You're not the Louvre out there, folks. A little hospitality wouldn't hurt.

triage.author: Benjamin
triage.title: If You’re Looking for North Dakota Hospitality, This Ain’t It.
triage.text: I’ve visited several presidential libraries across the country, including Lincoln in Springfield, Reagan in Simi Valley, and Nixon in Yorba Linda. None of them required timed tickets—you could simply walk in. So I drove hours out of my way to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora, North Dakota, only to be turned away at the door because I didn’t have a reservation. I explained the long drive and asked if there was any way to accommodate us, but the staff member seemed almost offended by the request and offered no sympathy or flexibility whatsoever. At twenty-six dollars a ticket and with the place clearly not crowded, that kind of attitude feels completely out of place for a destination this remote.

triage.author: Aspen Meissner
triage.text: The veil of "museum" on top of AI generated imperialist propaganda is so thin it may as well not be there. Unless you love AI slop and imperialism, do not come here.

triage.author: John Doe
triage.text: I’ve visited presidential libraries across the country—Lincoln, Reagan, Nixon—and walked right in, no timed tickets. Drove hours out of my way to the middle of nowhere in North Dakota to visit the @TRPresLibrary, where they’re charging twenty-six dollars to get in, and they still wouldn’t let me through the door without a reservation. Not busy, no flexibility, just ‘sorry, nope.’ You’re in rural North Dakota, not the Louvre looking at the Mona Lisa. Maybe dial down the attitude.

triage.author: Brandon Everett
triage.text: Careful verification of the location… if you don’t use the address in Google Maps it will take you to a random farm land an hour east of   Medora ND

triage.author: Judy J
triage.title: No customer service
triage.text: We purchased tickets for the museum, but needed to change them due to medical issues in our party. I sent an email 6 days ago and left a message 5 days ago. I tried the AI assistant today but it wasn’t any help. Apparently they don’t have any customer assistance staff. Extremely frustrating experience!

triage.author: Mark Z.
triage.text: Impossible to navigate to, was taken to the middle of a sunflower field. Never found the place.

triage.author: Haripriya G. Copple
triage.text:
Welp, I suppose people did this on purpose to mislead other people who wanted to visit Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library, Medora ND cz there was nothing but lands.
I hope people find this useful.

Edit: Thank you google for fixing it. Now it is fixed and people wont get lost and waste their time.

triage.author: Maureen D
triage.title: Very disappointed!
triage.text:
We were just turned away.  We arrived to Rough Rider SP on Monday, today is Wednesday.   Had we known we needed a TIMED TICKET we could have inquired.
THERE IS SOMETHING CALLED A VISITOR CENTER.  Not a single word, sign, flashing lights, etc, was at the Painted Canyon visitor center mentioning the library.  I don’t care if they are two different entities!  THERE SHOULD BE LIBRARY INFORMATION SOMEWHERE OTHER THAN THE WEBSITE, WHICH MY HUSBAND LOOKED AT.  HE DID NOT  SEE ANYTHING ABOUT A TIMED TICKET ON THE WEBSITE.
People come to the area and expect to get in.  We came from WY, almost 300 miles away. The library is HUGE!
Very disappointing!
I must say, the gentleman behind the counter took my displeasure very well, but he ruined our day!

triage.author: Corrine Krueger
triage.text: We weren't aware of the fact that you had to order your tickets in line. 🤔😭😢

triage.author: David Jenkins
triage.text: Reserve a time! Brand new. A lot of people . Teddy was a great president 👏, unlike....never mind.

triage.author: Karen Roberts
triage.text: Had some good areas to go thru.  They have an interactive program there. The kids seems to enjoy.  As an older person could have done without it. Also there are no exit signs pointing out of the building. Felt like we were in IKEA trying to get out.  Had a lot of good info. We didn't go up to the observation area.

triage.author: Benjamin Scott
triage.text: Drove hours out of my way to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora—because let’s be real, there’s not much else pulling people through that stretch of North Dakota. Got turned away at the door for not having a timed ticket. Explained the long drive, asked if there was any way to work with us, and the staff member looked almost insulted that I’d even asked. I’ve visited presidential libraries and the Smithsonian on the Fourth of July without this nonsense. You’re not the Louvre out there, folks. A little North Dakota hospitality would’ve gone a long way.

triage.author: Debbie Prado
triage.text: First of all, the pin on Google maps is NOT correct. It takes you southeast of Dickinson, down the Enchanted Highway to a dirt road,then another smaller dirt road that dead ends at two silos. As for the library, I was a bit disappointed but, glad they added some fun AI stuff. The area is beautiful and the staff very Kind. I got a peanut butter and jelly sandwich from the restaurant there and it was the worst I have ever had. Couldn't even eat it.

triage.author: Darla Hueske
triage.text:
Beautiful architecture blending into the landscape. Excellent views of the Medora valley.
All this gorgeous building and massive amount of money BUT NO North Dakota artists represented. The gift shop is filled with made in China junk.
Why? when there are so many amazing North Dakota artists that would represent our area.
Next why all the AI slop, when again there are many North Dakota artists to create an experience.
Do better Teddy team.

triage.author: Majid Shafiei
triage.text: Great design, poor construction. The design is inspires anyone that visits. However, 3 observations raise concern of shoddy execution or rushed completion. 1) Wood boards and wooden skin panels that were already lifting out of plane due to poor fastening, some showing recent repair attempts with mismatched screws. 2) rammed earth wall with extensive vertical cracking through multiple lifts, and crumbling sections along the bottom of lifts. I suspect this is due to uneven mixing (crumbling) or overly tight fastening to the underlying support structures which expand and settle at a different rate than the wall. 3) poured concrete floor at entrance to lobby with long cracks diagonally across the slab rather than in the joints. I'm no construction expert, but I encourage building professionals to take a look. It would be a shame if such an impressive design, with the power to revolutionize design in the US, were to become the example used to reinforce the unimaginative and unsustainable status quo.

triage.author: Tee M
triage.title: Innovative, Entertaining, but needs better crowd control!!!!
triage.text: We had a group of 10 visit this museum in August. We pre-purchased timed admission tickets for 12pm assuming it would help with crowd control since it had oy been open 6 weeks. The crowd was INSANE! We were elbow to elbow with a bazillion other people who were all fighting to maintain spots in line to try and enjoy each museum exhibit. You physically could not stop and read or interact with each station without someone pushing you or in front of you to see for themselves. It was a sad, aggressive, territorial scavenger hunt to try & protect your bubble to try and learn something. They need to do some sort of actual enforced timed, counted entry into each room to help alleviate the horrfic congestion during busy season, especially at the beginning of your experience. Towards the end of the afternoon, the crowd thinned out significantly, and we were able to retrace our steps and actually learn something. The interactive exhibits were innovative and entertaining for all ages in our group, which spanned 3 years old to 70. The Cafe stops serving early, which was a bummer because we spent so much time there due to crowds. Staff are not overly friendly or helpful. It's a beautiful, innovative, shiney new facility. We'd go back, just not in peak season.

triage.author: Dave K
triage.title: Great time and fascinating.
triage.text:
This presidential library was absolutely incredible! We visited with four adults and three kids, ages 6, 8, and 12, and every one of us was completely captivated. There was something to see, learn, and interact with around every corner, making it enjoyable for visitors of all ages.
The exhibits are thoughtfully designed with fascinating displays and hands-on experiences that kept everyone engaged. We found ourselves wanting to stop and explore every room, but unfortunately we had to leave sooner than we wanted because we had other plans in Medora.
This was easily one of the highlights of our trip, and it's one of those places you could visit more than once and still discover something new. We’re already looking forward to coming back so we can spend more time taking it all in! My only negative is the fact that adults are ages 13 on up. Where in this world is a 13 yr old an adult? Kind of crappy or them to charge this much for. a 13 yr old.

triage.author: Angela Thornburgh
triage.text: Great historical context and learning opportunities, beautiful grounds, and sustainable design in the spirit of Roosevelt himself. The exhibits are highly interactive and engaging for a range of ages with an animal "seek and find" for the youngsters, deeper policy and history related activities for everyone else, and cute historic/section-relevant AI photos for all ages. The tap-in passport style lets you navigate and understand easily if you missed anything. It makes navigation and completion a snap. I recommend making time to visit. Spend a few days and enjoy the full grounds, the National Park, and local attractions while you're there.

triage.author: Brayton Connard
triage.text: Great new library. Mix of artifacts and AI

triage.author: Tony Gabrielse
triage.text:
This is the first presidential library that I have visited, and it has set the bar incredibly high for an future presidential library visits!

This library is visually stunning, thoughtfully arranged, and extremely interactive and informative.  I was a little worried about how well our kids (ages 7, 11, and 14) would do at something like this, but we spent between 4-5 hours there without a single complaint.

I'd recommend buying tickets ahead of time to reserve a spot and save a few minutes on your way in.  When you arrive, there is free parking and then you head to the breezeway between the two buildings (library on one side and event and office space on the other).  You'll go through a security point before you enter and they do not allow any guns or knives of any sort in the building so I'd leave them in your car if you have them.

Once you enter you will get a bracelet to wear that has a chip in it that will give you access to all of the interactive parts of the library.  Then you'll register your bracelet with your name, email, and photo and head into the exhibits.  (The photo is for some some of the AI generated images. See pics below. But if you're worried big brother is watching, you can probably skip it if you want, but I'd highly recommend it.  Our kids thought it was awesome and hilarious.) You will get an email with your photos and also other parts of the experience that are a part of your "journal".

The exhibits walk through different phases of TR's life and experiences and lets you join in the experience in almost every area of the library.

TR and his family loved animals, so throughout the museum exhibits are animals you can try and find and scan with your bracelet to collect them all.  Our younger two had fun trying to find them all and it got them excited to travel from room to room.  Our 14 year old enjoyed the different interactive pieces of different exhibits too.

You can also do some walks outside and on the roof of the building!  Very fun and unique experience with incredible views.

If you're in the area, I can't recommend this place enough for you (and your family)! We did the library from 9-1:30, TR National Park from 2-5 (ate picnic lunch in the car), dinner from 5:30-6:30, and the Medora Musical to cap our day.  Great family trip! Hope you have as much fun as we did!

triage.author: Abbey&Max Oeser
triage.text:
Extremely well done, and the absolute gold standard for how all educational exhibits should be. The interactive experience is top tier and optional with the bracelets. You are able to “keep a journal” as you proceed and it will track all the fun exhibits you take part in.

It was by luck we ended up in Medora on July 8th 2026, and got to be some of the first to experience this absolute national treasure. If you are in the area, highly recommend you come and get the library experience.

I’m partially biased as I am a huge fan girl of Teddy, but this place is by far the most family friendly and interactive learning experience I’ve ever had the opportunity to partake in. There is so much beyond just reading and viewing exhibits. As you make your way through the library, you start to develop a sense of relationship with exactly who our 26th President was. It’s a really magically energy I can’t explain, you just need to go experience it yourself!

The price was reasonable for the experience, we spent about 3 hours in the library and I noted that I honestly would have paid double what we did, and could have doubled the time we spent inside.

We will be returning one day with our future (fingers crossed) kiddos to see how they let the land evolve around the building (it’s built INTO the landscape and has some amazing outdoor qualities to enjoy as well). A must see when experiencing the lands that made Teddy the man of conservation we know him to be.

triage.author: Kelli W
triage.text: The Roosevelt Library is truly a bucket list experience!! It is engaging for all ages and very educational. The interactive exhibits truly make you think and reflect. I left feeling inspired. The building itself and surrounding area is stunning and thoughtfully designed. May want to consider having arrows on the floor or signage to ensure guests follow the exhibits in chronological order. Overall, it was a wonderful experience!!

triage.author: R B
triage.title: Theodore Roosevelt Presidental Library. Great experience
triage.text: The library is worth th3 visit. Make a day of it. We were there a few hours and still did could have stayed longer, but it was very busy.  Staff is amazing.  Great historical esperience.

triage.author: Loring Fenn
triage.text: Very well done. GREAT interactive AI photos. Tremendous historical information about the man who pulled this country into a world leadership position.

triage.author: Sara Darby
triage.text: Absolutely loved this experience little overcrowded, but it was a great experience!

triage.author: Shelly Bailey
triage.text:
I would give more than 5 stars if I could. This facility was beyond amazing in the layout and systems used to present the life of TR. The scavenger hunt to find hidden animals and items throughout the museum was a fun add-on for people (even though I did not participate). It was great to see people’s reactions to their faces in the interactive displays too. Getting those photos at the end via email was nice, so definitely register your information at the beginning.

We spent 2 hours there which included our walk along the path. We could have spent 3 hours there though if I didn’t have other things planned for the day. Definitely recommend getting your tickets ahead of time - we did that and saw people getting turned away.  This is well worth the cost of a ticket.

triage.author: Mark Deschamp
triage.text: Very neat place!  Lots of history and interesting building, although the setting high on the bluff in the winter I wouldn't want to visit.

triage.author: Joe M.
triage.text: Really great experience here, they've done a fantastic job. You could easily spend a day here exploring both the museum and the walking paths outside but maybe not in the middle of summer when it's close to 100 degrees. The museum itself is a beautiful building with many artifacts and interactive parts. We have 2 young kids and they both enjoyed it. They did a good job of incorporating AI into the experience and you can get Gen AI pictures of yourself at various stages of TR's life. You can also interact with a hologram of TR and ask him questions. It's not an easy place to get to due to where it is located but it is worth it. We went on a Monday in July and while it was busy, we didn't have an issue getting tickets to go in.

triage.author: Lynn Schloesser
triage.text: The Library is a Great addition to the presentation of US history and a statement that in effect explains TRs presence on Mt. Rushmore. So glad this library is located in Medora ND where solitude and desolation can be briefly sampled, especially in Winter.   Look forward to comparisons with the Obama Presidential library that also opened this year.  The TR Library location and its story is epic.  Look forward to display of the equestrian statue now on site in storage on long term loan from the New York Natural History Museum. Look forward to a contextual display of the statue rooted in history, the TR ideal of constructive citizenship, without apology to public enthusiasms du jour.

triage.author: mel_pink5
triage.title: A true National treasure!
triage.text:
Awesome! Just plain awesome. Know when you go to go through the museum in order, it mimics his life story. I think the premise was to get people to wind through a certain way, but the big gallery room kinda confuses the flow. You will move front to back, and side to side as you progress. I think everyone is just so new they are figuring out things. 

In addition, the restaurant was closed for an event, and the gift shop only had $12 Cokes. There was one water fountain near the restrooms. They really need to rethink the needs of the customers when they are spending 3+ hours in the museum. Having water readily available, even if it is for purchase, is a must when you are in the Badlands. 

There is ample outside space to explore, great walking paths, and rocking chairs to enjoy the view (just need more). Parking filled up really fast, I hope they will develop more, and a shuttle from the far lots. 

All in all, this experience is fantastic, it is terrific for kids, take your time, enjoy the story!

triage.author: Stewart King
triage.text: An amazing museum with a comprehensive portrait of the man and his times. They did a good job of presenting the complexity and historical context. The exhibits were interesting, though they didn't actually have a lot of Roosevelt items; most of the documents and items they present are replicas of items that you can see in the original at Oyster Bay or (for the documents) at Harvard. I didn't do the interactive features but young people who were using them seemed to be amused; if I was there with kids I would certainly have participated. The architecture and grounds are fantastic! You get a good sense of the place and what it must have felt like to live here more than a century ago. What this is not is a library - Roosevelt's papers are at Harvard and even the tchotchke shop was very light on books. I was actually looking for Darren Lunde's The Naturalist, on Roosevelt's environmental initiatives, and didn't find it. The 25 bucks to get in was somewhat of a surprise but this is a private foundation, not the Park Service or the Archives, so be warned. Nevertheless, I recommend a visit to flesh out your experience in the stunning National Park next door.

triage.author: Vish Birbal
triage.text: Though more like a museum than a library, this was a fantastic experience! My wife and I loved the AI photos they made of us as well as the really cool mini-theaters detailing TR's Rough Riders and Brazilian river expedition. The AI conversation with the hologram was a bit glitchy but a cool concept overall.

triage.author: Noel F.
triage.text: The cost of admission here is worth every single penny. The building is beautiful, and it's unlike any museum I've ever experienced - top 5 for sure. There are so many interactive experiences throughout!! I don't want to spoil any fun, but there's a bracelet you wear with an RFID tag (think Disney magic band) that allows for activations throughout the exhibits. There's immersive videos, too, as well as an AI Teddy Roosevelt you can ask questions to (a partnership with Microsoft). It's genuinely just as fun as it is educational. I left with a new appreciation for what he did for conservation in the USA and a deeper understanding of his presidency and his life. The staff members were friendly if not a tad frazzled, given the heavy crowds. I'm not a history person but this was a highlight of my trip to North Dakota for sure.

triage.author: Richard Dixon
triage.text: Truly INCREDIBLE. Not only the best presidential library I have ever been to, but the best museum I have ever been to as well. The exhibits were so interactive and so much fun. The curators remembered that adults like to play and have fun too:). But truly so much fun for all ages. The AI photos were so amusing, as well as the games throughout and the immersive Amazon expedition. Very inspiring quote room and videos. And getting to actually ask a Teddy Roosevelt avatar questions??? So cool. My family and I had a blast. We all left truly feeling inspired to be better citizens and to do more and be better. So thoughtfully curated…the themes and interactive components all throughout. And Teddy’s real diary?? Insane. I loved the architecture and the obvious connection to nature. As the museum continues to refine its flow, I might recommend making it more clear to follow the timeline path of Teddy’s life. I also would have liked to see more about Alice Roosevelt and wondered why many pieces were not the originals, but replicas. Overall though, I will be highly recommending all to travel to Medora ND and experience the beautiful and inspiring Teddy Roosevelt Presidential Library and Museum.

triage.author: Kayne Phillips
triage.text: Nice library with good exhibits. Great job giving the history of president Roosevelt. Managed to make it interesting for adults and young kids. Timed tickets but I wish they'd reduce the number of people allowed in at a time as it was crowded and many people can't seem to figure out how to follow the flow of the exhibits making it more annoying.

triage.author: Matt Roelfs
triage.text: Incredibly engaging and fun. The exhibits and videos are really good. I think the interactive TR was neat too. I appreciate the timed entry although it's not really enforced. It was busy but not too bad. I highly recommend!

triage.author: Allen T
triage.title: Don't pass it by
triage.text: The very model of a modern presidential museum (not really a library). Probably the best single attraction in North Dakota....the state should promote it heavily. Building, exhibits and connection to the landscape are outstanding, even if I might have a few quibbles with the museum's interpretations of TR's career. And who doesn't love those AI-generated photos they send you!

triage.author: Gayle Birkenheier
triage.text: Recently opened on July 4 this year it is a beautiful display of architecture that meets nature and its surrounding area. We did not go inside as we had dogs but I hear it is beautiful. Landscape is amazing

triage.author: David Fisher
triage.text: An amazing experience. Weather was 101 degrees outside was the only downside. It was super busy but it's brand new.

triage.author: Jesse
triage.text:
This is a well constructed museum experience, though I don't know enough to know if it constitutes a "Presidential Library". Some of the experiences and moments of Theodore Roosevelt's life are very well orchestrated, such as the presentation of his tragic loss and the diary entry after. Some of the experiences felt less than they could have been with the computer generated/AI elements. I did not interact with the AI Teddy because it feels hollow and not worth the time, with all the other moments being more impactful.

There is some sad irony in the trust-busting and monopoly-fighting that TR did alongside the nature of how this place came together, as well as the current push to take, end, or sell public lands to the highest bidders which Teddy probably would be turning in his grave over.

The (literal) windows to the Badlands sprinkled throughout  the walking experience were well architected and planned.  The walk along the roof and the building melding into the Badlands is well done.

triage.author: Andreas Obrecht
triage.text: The library is great, we enjoyed the architecture and the exhibition. The only downside was the the on-site restaurant was closed (no accurate info on website!) and the interactive journal was never sent.

triage.author: Highwayknight
triage.text: Great historical contributions about the 26th president. The interactive items were pretty kool. But, there should be a shuttle system for those that have to park far away and are disabled.

triage.author: Jamie H. Wellik
triage.text:
Wow!  Impressive location, building, amenities and displays.  It’s been over a month and they are getting better handling large crowds, older visitors and ushering through the entire museum experience (admission, security, lockers, dining, etc.)

I can’t remember last time I felt so moved- and impressed- by the displays in a museum- the curators did an excellent job incorporating modern historians and politicians into the legacy of Theodore Roosevelt.

And the gift shop needs a huge book selection….

triage.author: Ray Magill
triage.text:
I have edited and changed my review to 5 stars.  Although all that I said below was true. It appears their system did work eventually and
I received my journal .  The library experience itself is definitely 5 star.

I would dearly love to give 5 stars for this truly informative and unique place about my favorite president.  But I am greatly disappointed that all of the memories they promise to email to us failed to materialize.  All of the other members of our party received theirs and it is a nice memory.  Neither myself nor my wife received ours.  Furthermore we knew before we left the area so returned to the information desk.  They had a specific QR code to scan that allowed notification of this failure and supposedly retrieve your memory email.  So obviously this is not a new problem.
Nothing.
I also left message at their phone number and sent message thru their website.
Again nothing.
They want to promote their AI experience which was pretty cool but then fail on the most important personal connection to the library.  I hope they figure this out so as to not disappoint other visitors.  Visitors should follow-up with them prior to departure so they can double check that their system is working .

triage.author: Daniel Randolph
triage.text:
Spectacular.This is the newest high tech and immersive Presidential Library yet.

Display are cool and lots of AI enhance to help you heel you are in the room.

There is a really good press briefing where you can ask any question and probably answer correctly.

Also, the building is vet cool architecture that perfectly complements the bad lands. The trail on the roof is amust

triage.author: Seth
triage.text: Went today and it was a great experience!!!! So cool. It was huge. You can spend hours in there. It is very busy though and crowded but still a great experience. So glad I live in North Dakota and close to this where I can go back when ever I want !!! Highly recommend!!!

triage.author: Lakeisha Heeringa
triage.text:
Can I give it 10 stars?
We road tripped out to ND for the Badlands and thought we'd stop in at the Presidential Library because it was there. Good thing we were smart enough to buy tickets the night before!
The place was packed and I understand why!
The exhibits were fabulous!!! There were things to do and see for all ages. Museum artifacts, interactive exhibits, scavenger hunts, replicas, rooms designed to immerse you in different eras of TR's life... there was just so much. I do highly recommend the AI wristbands and interactive exhibits... which is saying something for me, because I'm normally not a fan of a lot of AI stuff.
Bottom line: I'm sad the Presidential Library is 13 hours from home because I would go often!

My only critique is there wasn't enough stuff in the gift shop. If you're looking to buy books written by Teddy Roosevelt, you're better off going to the national park gift shop.

Also, FYI, if someone in your party needs to use the restroom bad, the bathrooms are on the other side of the security line.

triage.author: Jami Schwab
triage.text: This place is amazing! I could spend quite a bit of time there. I need to go back and go through slower to take in more of the education. The technology is so great. The kids loved all the AI activities. Make sure you use the bathroom at entrance, especially the kids, there is not another one until the end and it only has a few stalls.

triage.author: PhillipABukowski
triage.title: Overcrowded during peak season
triage.text:
The library is a 10/10 experience but they’re overselling the tickets for admission and the place is packed with bottlenecks at all of the interactive exhibits. 

If you can come during “off season” it’ll be absolutely amazing. 

Also the gift shop is brutally overpriced. And the bathrooms are too small for the crowds. Beware.

triage.author: SuburbanMomof2kids
triage.title: It’s more than a library
triage.text: Definitely a unique and fun experience. Once inside, the fresh wood furniture smell is evident. We got bracelets as part of the experience for interactive exploring. Make sure you use it to tap the many photo ops and seek and find animals to log your own personal online journal. Once you take your photo at the beginning, it’s used to create these Theodore Roosevelt period, black and white portraits. Pretty cool. Each exhibit is educational and entertaining. Lots to see and take in. Very awe inspiring and showcased Roosevelt’s accomplishments and contributions to America’s greatness. He had so many inspiring quotes that were used throughout the library. It took us 3 hours easily and we don’t think we covered all. Must visit before it gets too popular. It got very crowded as people came and stayed. Food wasn’t great, maybe they will improve. Souvenirs were pricey even for a postcard. Surrounding canyon sights were magnificent. Glad we drove 4 hours from Mt Rushmore to get there.

triage.author: Abby H
triage.title: First Time Visitor
triage.text: Wow! What an experience. I was gifted tickets without any prior knowledge of what to expect. I have visited many museums, and this by far, exceeded my expectations. The interactive exhibits made it engaging for young children and an incredible educational experience. In no time, three hours had escaped us. If you have mobility issues, I highly recommend being dropped off at the front entrance and riding the golf cart to the front door. Most likely, there will be a line to stand in even if you have purchased tickets ahead of time. Once you make it through the first exhibit, there is adequate seating options to rest at before venturing to other exhibits. Try to bring as little as possible so your hands won’t be tied up and you can easily access the interactive exhibits. There are clean restrooms available upon walking in and within the main area. Food is available on site too. Plan in your budget to find something at the gift shop! A lot of great options to find a keepsake of your experience.

triage.author: Traci
triage.text: Wow, this is really well done and surpassed my expectations. Very busy, would love to visit when less busy to fully get through the areas and take more time. Recommended to by tickets for a time slot ahead of time.

triage.author: Russell Waters
triage.text: This is an amazing place. It is a must see. He was a great man and they did a great job telling the story of his life.  Buy tickets ahead and allow at least 3 hours.

triage.author: Jeff Iverson
triage.text:
Museum is well laid out. A great learning experience for kids. Beautiful location.
One thing is the ticket lady was CRABBBY when I gave her my ticket and was too early.

triage.author: Kris B
triage.text:
We stopped yesterday to visit. Unfortunately, the line was so long we were only able to explore the outside grounds.
That's okay, though, because what we saw was impressive. Kudos to President Roosevelt for building a library that doesn't detract from the surroundings. In fact, this library is built into the surroundings.
We'll be back someday. We've explored outside, so next time we'll be sure to explore inside.

triage.author: Karen F.
triage.text:
We came at the beginning of August to tour the new TR presidential library. This was my first presidential library and all I can say is wow! I don't even know what to start with from how beautiful the building is to all of the amazing exhibits. This place is truly one of a kind. I honestly could've spent hours in there. 

I wish I would've had more time. It's new as it just opened a month ago so obviously it was very very busy . I love to see everyone so excited about history. I don't know when I'll ever get back to Medora again, but this was probably the highlight of the trip.

I went with some of my nieces And it was really fun viewing the museum through their eyes. Particularly the interactive room with TR where you can ask him all sorts of questions that was just so educational. I can see why this museum took so long to come to fruition. But it's absolutely superb.

I would say my favorite room is what we called the train room. All of the love letters written on the walls were so endearing to read. I was also lucky enough to see his actual Journal that will only be on display for a short period  of time.

triage.author: panpanda
triage.title: One of the best museums I've ever seen!
triage.text:
Fantastic! This new museum uses lots of new tricks to make history come alive. 
First, they take your photo when you enter and then send you amazing AI generated photos placing you in historical photos. Amazing! 
Many replicas are not displayed under glass  so you can touch them. 
There are fabulous films with first rate technology. The one at the end, of Theodore and his son's journey to the Amazon at the end of his life is unbelievably good. 
One of the best museums I've ever seen. It just opened July 4 and is crowded, so buy your tickets in advance

triage.author: Vicki Bunkelman
triage.text: Too many people here on the day we went. But it us brand new so I suppose that is expected.  Did not get to spend much time on things because of so many  people wanting to see the same things. Doing all the activities I felt rushed to keep moving.

triage.author: Karen M
triage.text:
What an excellent experience. There's so much to see and learn.  Unfortunately some of it gets lost with patrons seeing themselves in vintage photos that are posted throughout the venue.  I would not recommend it for very young children.
The design of the library takes your breath away when you first see it. Blends right into the landscape.

triage.author: Kath Williams
triage.text: Fabulous!! We used every bit of 4 hours. The guided tour is wonderful. Glen was awesome! I highly recommend!! Prepare for a wait even when you pre purchase tickets. Security line outside and entrance line inside. It is a long time to stand in line. I hope they figure something better for their customers.

triage.author: Julie Teberg
triage.text: We spent some time at the library.   The building is breathe taking.   It blends in with the surroundings so beautifully.   Since the library just opened in July, you can imagine the crowds of people but once we were inside you could spread out and see everything.   I look forward to going back again to see it.  Be sure to get your tickets online before you go

triage.author: Wesley Smith
triage.text: Was pretty cool.  More high tech than expected.  Some of the tech wasn't working already, haha...money well spent by the gvt.  Interesting design.  Nice little walking look and good views.

triage.author: Jason Uhlmann
triage.text: A great experience for a truly great President! Be sure to book in advance. They even have free car chargers, although they are often blocked by those who don’t get it and could use some signage.

triage.author: Carl Strohmeyer
triage.text:
Excellent experience.
Unique interactive exhibits.
A bit crowded and busy, but we went only one month after opening.

triage.author: Terry Bishop
triage.text:
Since we were traveling across North Dakota we wanted to visit the TR Presidential Library, we bought tickets online 2 days in advance to make sure we could get in, they have time slots and we took a 10a, when we got there they were already busy,  the website says August is a busy month in Medora and they expect the Library to be busy also and it was!
We spent a couple hours wandering around and could spend more time but couldn't.
My wife and me agreed we need to return another time before memorial day or a week or so after Labor day
and hopefully it won't be so busy.
They also have a some big rocking chairs at the end of the breezeway where you can sit, relax and look at the ND badlands

triage.author: Rhonda
triage.text:
The New Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library was very interesting and full of history of this area and the politics of that time.  We fully appreciate Pres. Roosevelt establishing many National Parks for us to enjoy.  Dislike how the Native Americans were treated during his Presidency.

The architecture of the Library was very interesting!  We did not like how they are charging admission to the library.  Did not see the need to spend that much money that  the people would then have to pay for admission to the library.  If it sits on nearly 100 acres maybe could have been just as beautiful on 20 acres.  Many of the displays were wonderful and others were just put in to allow kids to play.  A lot of cost could have been removed so not to have to charge.

triage.author: Melinda Gholson
triage.text: Really a fantastic place. Our only complaint is that we couldn't see every detail due to the crowds. Get your tickets in advance and choose a morning time if possible. Hopefully the crowds will be smaller then. The exhibits were wonderful and touched on all parts of Roosevelt's life. What an educational experience for me. I loved the movie about Teddy's trip in the amazon. The interactive exhibits which allow you to insert your photo into the scene were amazing. Everything about the library is amazing. Well done, bravo! We especially loved seeing Teddy's authentic diary on display in a carefully lit room -- opened to the page where he wrote a huge X after the death of his mother and beloved wife on the same day. There is so much to see and do in this venue. If I could do it again, I would visit on two separate days, with hikes in-between. It's a four-hour venue but the human body is just built for two-hour max museum visits. So .... when planning your trip ... worth it to plan for two visits.

triage.author: Den Mac
triage.text:
I have to keep reminding myself this place only opened in July. The concept is good and the place is beautiful. However, there are flow issues inside. There needs to be better signage to match the map for timeline accuracy visiting of the different areas.
While there are a lot of beautiful artifacts, the description placards contain too small of print & some of the placards have words worn off already.
In the gift shop, I think maybe they didn't plan to be so busy because they were sold out of some basic items such as TR Library stickers.

In the cafe, they could be more efficient if they would have a menu visible from the line instead of not until you get to the counter. Very beautiful grounds and conveniently located near the Medora Musical.

triage.author: Maria Vargas-Salazar
triage.text:
Amazing experience. The interactive activities for all ages was amazing. Teddy Roosevelt was an amazing president who developed our country beautifully.  His life experiences and such a young age. He was our youngest president at age 42!  Definitely a future trivia question.  The building structure and care for the surrounding nature would have made the president proud.

Lots of walking!!!!!!! So be prepared.
Not very much space for RV parking.

The beautiful town of Medora does have a RV parking lot and offer a shuttle to the library if that works for you.

Some fun interactive pics generated at the library. Grounds pics and different galleries that explain his life.   Lots of amazing history and storytelling. Enjoy!

triage.author: Damon Horn
triage.text:
The location is absolutely beautiful and the architecture is breathtaking. The trails are a very pleasant and the site was clearly set up with care. The exhibits are engaging and use technology well. I only have 2 complaints:

1) It took around 30-40 minutes to get in. The line was moving very slowly because the digital check in kiosks took a while.

2) I asked the AI Teddy Roosevelt a question ("Did you support Eugene Debs imprisonment for protesting the draft?") The computer had to think for a long time, then basically said that while he disagreed with Debs, freedom of speech is important and he should have the right to say what he wants. I researched the exact question later and found that TR had said many negative things specifically about Debs and had written in support of jailing people for opposing WWI and the draft. It was disappointing to have received inaccurate information in the library, and a reminder that AI can be tricky and overconfident. I wish the AI exhibit had simply said it didn't know the answer instead of making something up that didn't fit the facts.

Alternatively you could have a docent or TR impersonator answer questions, which I have seen work well at other museums.

Despite these two quibbles, the museum is overall excellent and I enjoyed myself.

triage.author: Roy Smith
triage.text: Be aware that Google maps sends you to some spot over 50 miles away. Use Medora as destination then follow signs until Google fixes that. We discovered apple maps did take you to the correct location.

triage.author: Jill Lee
triage.text: Amazing museum.  Fantastic information.   Must order tickets before arrival.  We were there for two days.  Sometimes very crowded, but museum handles crowds very well.  AMAZING INTERACTIVE DISPLAYS.

triage.author: Kelly Rounds
triage.text: Fantastic museum. The way it's laid out is the best and you can actually touch things. The staff is very informative and nice to visit with. The only thing I can say negative and really is not the Librarys fault Google maps will send you a hour and twenty minutes the wrong way and will have you in a wheat field. Staff says they have been trying to get Google to change it but they won't.

triage.author: gramma of many
triage.title: Wonderful Experience !
triage.text:
Cannot even begin to describe how wonderful this place is! 
Beautifully done, very interactive and use of AI with photography. You will get several keepsake photos of your experience. You will also get to ask Teddy live questions and he answers…. Just unbelievable! 
Plenty for children to interact with; scavenger hunt for animals through out is fun for kids. Plan to spend at least 4 hours! We didn’t want to leave!
Cafe is delicious and priced fair.
 Only disappointing thing was gift shop… very little to choose from, few books, one or two shirts and 2 sweatshirts to choose from… no stickers!
Beautiful setting with outdoor rocking chairs to enjoy the badlands 
I’d recommend reading “ mornings on horseback “ before you go and the museum will come alive. 
I loved it so much, I will visit again!!

triage.author: Jane Burriss
triage.text: The lines are long and the staff are still figuring out what to do. It's a great place, but there are some start-up frustrations. They have lots of interactive things that will keep the attention of all ages.

triage.author: Shana Beattie
triage.text: Beautiful tribute to our former President. Very informative engaging for both adults and children. But please plan at least 3-4 hours to take everything in, including enjoying the outdoors scenery. Starting at 4pm wasn’t enough time.

triage.author: BRS
triage.text: Walk the rooftop path instead of watching all the AI nonsense.  What do think TR would do?

triage.author: Billy Rendeluk
triage.text: Too much to see in a single visit.  The majority of exhibits are interactive so plan to arrive early.  There is a magnatron security check point before entering so it would be advised to look up the library ahead of the visit to learn which items are prohibited.  If you use the airport security protocol you should be okay.  Restrooms are available during the tour but no water fountains were seen.  This is a cashless site so carry your card(s).

triage.author: f stavins
triage.text: Very well done. Do not miss the AI Theodore. The setting was perfect. Timed tickets  in advance of visit was helpful. Good restaurant but closes early.

triage.author: J U2
triage.text: Tickets only available online. Worth the time and there are many “passport” activities and photo memories to receive free, but email and general information is needed. This is done right as you enter with timed tickets. Plenty of parking- some covered. Morning is less crowded than midday or late afternoon. Countless displays to read and see. We spent 4 hours and could have spent more and if you like history it’s a fantastic experience.

triage.author: Brian Reynolds
triage.text:
Superb museum with tons of exhibits and artifacts.

The interactive wrist bands make the museum come to life with AI blended photographs.

Exceptionally well done.  The only downside are the fellow museum goers who are oblivious to others in the museum.

triage.author: Ellen White
triage.text:
Problem is with the roads leading to and from the parking lot are not marked well
The inside of the building is fabulous

triage.author: BBooker
triage.title: Bully!
triage.text:
Great experience. Seems like most complaints are due to the timed entry tickets. Well, it opened only in late July, so I understand.   It was very clear on the website. Crowds were tolerable. Lots of reading to do, with rows and rows of displays aboutTR’s life, chronologically.
So, sometimes delays. Many video features to give you a break from the reading. Much AI involved. Interesting to see where that technology is here in 2026. Only negative:  Avoid the restaurant at all costs. High prices, low quality, slow service.

triage.author: Erica C
triage.title: Overwhelmed
triage.text: Very impressed by architecture.      Parking was a nightmare.  There were campers parked in vehicle parking spots. Apparently no one is monitoring the parking lots. Also we purchased tickets ahead of time thinking that they were limiting the number of people in the library however it was very crowded.  Lots of information and I learned a lot. However the room dedicated to his childhood was very dark. I wish it had been lit better so we could see things.

triage.author: IowaTraveler925
triage.title: Take the whole day - hope it's one of the best museums ever for you too!
triage.text:
Our trip to the Badlands (ND and SD) was driven by 2 things - the new Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library and the Sturgis Mustang Rally (the later of which drove the timing). 

I am a big US Presidential history geek and thankfully my husband doesn't mind joining me on our various adventures to such libraries. 

We became members of the Library before coming, an investment we will likely continue based on our impressive experience. 

HIGHLY recommend getting timed entry tours and any specialty tour tickets before you arrive. Also recommend allowing time (weather permitting) for exploring the grounds and the museum's rooftop prairie.

We kicked our day off with a guided highlights tour pre-booked. It was a perfect lay of the landscape overview for the intensive, immersive Museum experience.

I deeply appreciate how transparent this facility is in identifying what is an authentic, original artifact and what is a replica. History geek coming out, I know. 

We shared an entree in their Native American themed on site restaurant, Salt & Scoria. Tasty! FYI, their kiosks have a more extensive and complete menu than the beautifully hand written menu that hangs in the restaurant.

Our timed entry tickets followed 1.5 hours after our guided highlights tour, which was just enough time to grab a little lunch before going in. The Museum is well-equipped with staff to help you setup your virtual experiences and get properly checked in. The sold out day we joined (a Saturday) made for shoulder to shoulder experiences - crowded - but almost all kind and considerate humans, thankfully. 

I'd recommend any fellow history geek allow for at LEAST 4 hours for the main museum exhibits and attractions. 

We also added on a late afternoon TR Deep Dive tour. While there was little content overlap between the two tours, our guide for the latter tour was less prepared/more nervous. He might have been new, in fairness - the museum just opened in July and our first guide has been closely involved with the Museum for 5+ years.

This museum is immersive, intensive, beautiful and wonderfully fact focused. Could not recommend the trip any higher!

triage.author: Patti Clark
triage.text: Highly recommend.  Make sure you do the registration at the beginning so that you can more fully participate in all the interactive AI.  You will get an email after your visit recording some of the things you did.  There are glitches though.  I did not receive my email, but others in my party did.  Four hours wasn't enough time to do and see all that was available.  I hope to be able to go back sometime.

triage.author: Gail Olson
triage.text: Great museum. Recommend late morning/early afternoon arrival to avoid crowds. Numerous interactive exhibits which can be downloaded to your e-mail.

triage.author: lynne shenk
triage.text: Fantastic. The views on the outside were great, and the exhibits on the inside were fun, interactive and very informative. Arrive early as check-in is a bit slow.

Careful verification of the location… if you don’t use the address in Google Maps it will take you to a random farm land an hour east of   Medora ND

I’ve visited several presidential libraries across the country, including Lincoln in Springfield, Reagan in Simi Valley, and Nixon in Yorba Linda. None of them required timed tickets—you could simply walk in. So I drove…

One star for the outdoors and the architecture which was great. Otherwise it’s just ai bullshit with replicas of the real things everywhere. I can’t in good faith recommend anyone go to this place. It’s a Presidental lib…
Great place to visit and learn all about TR.  Very interactive and they create a photo journal.  Great layout and friendly staff.
This NP is amazing to explore. We had so much fun seeing wild horses 🐎  tons of bison 🦬 and of course the whimsical prairie dogs.

Recently opened on July 4 this year it is a beautiful display of architecture that meets nature and its surrounding area. We did not go inside as we had dogs but I hear it is beautiful. Landscape is amazing
Very neat place!  Lots of history and interesting building, although the setting high on the bluff in the winter I wouldn't want to visit.

7.headline: Ratings easing to 4.64 across 48 reviews
paragraphs: 48 reviews in the last 7 days, down 1 on the previous 7 days. The average is down 0.03. 8.5% rated three stars or below.

Visitors are consistently praising the interactive exhibits, the building and the setting. The AI experience continues to divide a small minority: 58 reviews to date name it as the reason for a low rating, against heavy praise for the same feature. Low volume, but it is the most likely subject of a critical feature story.

The complaints that cost us stars cluster tightly. The most frequent is confusion about timed entry (3 mentions), followed by crowding inside the galleries and the food offer. These are operational and messaging fixes rather than problems with the experience itself, which is the better problem to have. Separately, 99 reviews are waiting on a reply and 85 are past our own service level.
notes: 20 reviews predate public opening, averaging 4.4. These are press, donor and Founding Member previews. They count toward all-time figures but are held out of the response queue.
